# Project plan

The project will be developed in a public GitHub repository under the MIT licence, with issues used to track all work.

## Technical delivery
<!--
Covering the actual delivery of the project this section should
provide at least a high-level description of the implementation.

Including target dates is really important as you need to be committed
and the ISC need to have a means of tracking delivery
-->

I've given Vale a trial run over an existing R package to test out comment extraction. The results were noisy but workable. It picks up comments from R source files with correct line numbers and handles vignettes and READMEs without any extra work.

### Milestone 1 - 31st January 2027: working package and first rules

This milestone starts with talking to package maintainers and reading through documentation feedback in public software review threads, such as rOpenSci's, to decide which rules are most useful in the default style.
The code delivered is the R package that installs or locates Vale, runs it over a package and returns lints as a data frame, with an initial set of rules and snapshot tests, working on Linux, macOS and Windows.

### Milestone 2 - 28th February 2027: default style and release

This milestone covers the remaining rules, the vocabulary of R terms, and the setup function that writes the Vale config and the AGENTS.md block, with each rule documented with examples of what passes and what fails.
The style is run over the 100 most downloaded CRAN packages and the results used to tune the rules and defaults.
The package goes to CRAN and the style is published so Vale users can install it directly, with documentation covering use from R, from the command line, and on CI via Vale's existing GitHub Action and pre-commit hook.
The project is written up for the R Consortium blog.

All code is MIT licensed and developed in the open on GitHub. The package will go to CRAN and the style will be published on GitHub so it can be used with Vale directly.
Publicity is a post on the R Consortium blog, posts on LinkedIn, Mastodon and Bluesky at each milestone, and a submission to R Weekly.

The budget is labour only, at USD 90 per hour, for 40 hours of part-time work over two months.
There are no other costs. GitHub covers hosting, CI and releases.

| 2: Default style and release | 28 Feb 2027 | 20 | 1,800 |
| **Total** | | **40** | **3,600** |
